title: Formal and Informal Register
summary: Adjust grammar, pronouns, contractions, and vocabulary to match Brazilian social and professional contexts.

sections.heading: Pronouns and address
sections.body: Brazilian Portuguese generally uses **você** in both informal and many professional contexts. Formality is often shown through vocabulary, complete forms, titles, and politeness strategies rather than switching to a different 'you'.

examples.pt: Você poderia me enviar o arquivo?
examples.en: Could you send me the file?

examples.pt: Prezada Ana, encaminho o relatório solicitado.
examples.en: Dear Ana, I am forwarding the requested report.

sections.heading: Grammar and contractions
sections.body: Informal speech accepts reductions and looser pronoun placement. Formal writing prefers full forms, standard object pronouns or clear noun phrases, and fewer colloquial markers.

examples.en: I'll send it to you tomorrow.
I will send it to you tomorrow.

sections.heading: Politeness without stiffness
sections.body: Professional Brazilian Portuguese values clarity and warmth. Conditional forms, indirect requests, and gratitude soften messages without sounding overly formal.

examples.pt: Fico à disposição para esclarecer dúvidas.
examples.en: I remain available to answer questions.

keyPoints: Formality in Brazil is often lexical and pragmatic, not just pronoun-based.
Use full forms and standard spelling in formal writing.
Você can be polite when paired with poderia, por favor, and appropriate tone.
Avoid colloquial reductions in official emails, academic writing, and résumés.

commonMistakes.right: Você poderia enviar o documento, por favor?

commonMistakes.note: Do not mix a gente with plural verb agreement.
